title: Adaptive KV-prefetch + routing PRD scratchpad (Noah Kim)
content:
Context / elevator pitch:
We observe a common pattern: many user sessions send repeated, similar prompts or have deterministic prefix tokens (system messages, user metadata) that could benefit from targeted KV-cache prefetching. Combine lightweight request routing signals (route, user tier, model variant, input prefix fingerprint) to opportunistically prefetch KV blocks into the serving runtime and reduce p95/p99 latency and token cost per request (by enabling more aggressive batching and cache hits).

This doc is a rough PRD / brainstorm. Notes are informal — TODOs and open questions scattered.

Problem statement:
- Cold-start token latency and token-level compute remains a significant pain for short, interactive use-cases (chat replies, code completions).
- Existing global prefix caching helps but is coarse; we waste GPU cycles recomputing KV for slightly different prefixes or user-specific system prompts.
- When a request routes to a lower-cost model variant (quantized), we may still be able to reuse parts of the KV cache but current routing lacks a prefetch signal.

Goals (success metrics):
- Reduce median and p95 generation latency for typical 8–64 token completions by 10–25% on targeted routes within 3 months of rollout.
- Increase KV-cache hit-rate for prefetchable prefixes by 20% on instrumented routes.
- Net cost delta <= +5% (or ideally cost-neutral) — goal is latency improvement, not big cost increases.
- Low operational complexity: feature must be controllable per-route with conservative defaults.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full rewrite of routing or autoscaling. Keep it incremental and opt-in per route/customer.
- Not targeting massive long-sequence batch workloads initially.

User personas / stories:
- Product engineer (chat feature): "I want consistent sub-200ms interactive responses for short replies without over-provisioning GPUs."
  - Acceptance: When enabled on my route, observed p50/p95 latency improves on dev traffic within 2 weeks; no user-visible correctness regressions.
- Platform engineer / SRE: "I want visibility and kill-switches: per-route toggles, telemetry, and fail-open behavior."
  - Acceptance: Buttons/flags exist in the Console, and we can disable prefetching per pool/route; rollout supports canary.
- Enterprise customer (sensitive data): "I want prefetching to respect KMS/HSM and not leak prefixes across tenants."
  - Acceptance: Prefetch respects routing isolation and tenant boundaries; options to only prefetch encrypted session KV under private deployments.

Feature sketches / components:
1) Prefetch policy model (simple rules engine):
   - Inputs: route id, user tier, model id/variant, prefix fingerprint (hash of first N tokens), recent session traffic histogram, time-of-day, explicit route config (enabled/disabled, aggressive/conservative).
   - Output: whether to prefetch, which KV shards or token ranges, priority (low/medium/high), TTL.

2) Runtime prefetcher shim (serving-runtime):
   - Lightweight actor that receives prefetch requests and warms KV caches in the GPU process without blocking the main request path.
   - Should be asynchronous and rate-limited per pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

3) Router integration + Console controls:
   - Route config toggle: prefetch={off, on, aggressive} with per-route quota and burst cap.
   - Dashboard: prefetch hits, prefetch attempts, prefetch latency, cost delta.

4) Fingerprinting & heuristics:
   - Fingerprint based on first 6–16 tokens or normalized system prompt. Configurable length.
   - Heuristics: always prefetch for exact-match fingerprints above X occurrences/min or for routes with high short-completion ratio.

5) Safety & tenant isolation:
   - Prefetch only within route/tenant scope. For private deployments, honor network/KMS constraints.
   - Logging & audit for all prefetch operations.

Operational controls / rollout plan:
- Phase 0: offline simulation using traces (run prefetch policy on historical request logs to estimate hit rate and overhead).
- Phase 1: internal canary on non-prod routes (opt-in). Monitor hit rate and GPU cycles consumed.
- Phase 2: gradual rollout to select customer routes with Console toggle + alerting.
- Phase 3: wide rollout with defaults conservative (off) and templates for common chat routes.

Metrics to measure:
- Prefetch attempts / minute, prefetch hit-rate (% of prefetched KV used by subsequent request within TTL).
- Delta in p50/p95 generation latency for targeted routes.
- GPU utilization delta attributable to prefetching (separate metric to detect waste).
- Cost per 1k completions before/after.

Open questions / risks (to resolve):
- How to choose TTL for prefetched KV without wasting memory? (idea: TTL adaptive based on fingerprint recurrence frequency)
- Backpressure: how aggressively can prefetching run during P95 load spikes? Need robust rate limits per pool.
- Interaction with batching: prefetching could enable bigger batch windows for future requests — positive, but need careful instrumentation.
- Model compatibility: some encoder-decoder / instruction-tuned variants might not share identical KV semantics — how to detect compatibility?
- Privacy/regulatory: ensure prefetch does not cause cross-tenant leakage — design isolation first.

Rough technical tasks (brainstorm TODOs):
- [ ] Build offline simulator that scans 30 days of request logs and computes fingerprint recurrence and potential hit rate. (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Prototype runtime prefetch actor in serving runtime (owner: Emma). Minimal API: prefetch(prefix_hash, model_variant, priority).
- [ ] Console UI mock: per-route toggle + charts (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Define telemetry spec (metrics, traces, alerts) and add to product observability backlog.
- [ ] Security review for private deployments and KMS interaction.

Quick sketch of acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Prefetch policy can be enabled per-route and respects per-pool rate limits.
- Offline simulator shows >15% potential hit-rate for at least 2 identified routes.
- Runtime prefetcher warms KV without increasing request tail latency (i.e., async no-block by design).
- Console exposes per-route toggle + top-level prefetch metrics.

Notes to self / ideas to consider later:
- Could pair with user/session-level warmers for known scheduled events (e.g., live support shifts).
- Integrate with Optimize: recommend prefetch config when workload shows high short-completion ratio.
- Consider ML-based policy if simple rules underperform — maybe predict next-prefix probability from session context.

Links / references:
- Related scratchpads: users/llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json (check for overlaps)
- JIRA: INF-789 (prefetch simulation backlog)
- Slack thread: #runtime-prefetch (see pinned messages)

Next steps (this week):
- Run quick offline pass on last 7 days of chat traffic and produce a short metrics snapshot (hit-rate estimate by fingerprint length).
- Schedule 30m sync with Emma + Jordan + Priya to agree MVP scope and owners.
- Draft initial Console mock and share in #product-optimize for feedback.

-- end scratchpad --
